about: slapstic page 3 $85EC-$97FF: the TIE fighters of wave part 3, Star Wars' space wave code with ESB's changes - set-up for the game and for the training manual, view and lazar test of the ships, the computer pilots with their choreography interpreter, the wave and choreography tables - then a stale copy of part of that code ($9361-$9560) and the player's lazars: the start of a shot, the beams and the walker part's collision test

P3:85EC.name: tie_wave_init
P3:85EC.desc: page 3 half of the set-up of the TIE fighter part (wave3_setup, phase $47), made from the alien loop of Star Wars' IPGEN: starts at level 0 of the wave set (WV_LVL), gives each of the three alien records its unit vector block (M_AL on, $20 apart) and block index (MS_ALBC on, 4 apart), marks it dead and sets its fire delay (byte 4, ESB's addition to the record) to 8. NWNSHP_P3 then makes the first ships

P3:8613.name: man_tie_setup
P3:8613.desc: set-up for the TIE fighter pages of the training manual, called by man_init_tie (which passes the page number in B, not used here): initialises the three alien records as tie_wave_init does, then makes the first one a live TIE fighter by hand, the way NWASHP does - unit vectors facing the player, placed at x $1000, y 0, z 0, 1 hit, the choreography man_tie_chor, which keeps it in place while it yaws, pitches and rolls, and object 0 loaded through bank 1 KD868

P3:8A86.name: tie_fire_delay
P3:8A86.desc: ESB's addition to the loop of CPU, X = alien record: counts the ship's fire delay (byte 4 of the record) down by one a frame until it is 0. CPUAL lets the ship fire only when it is 0 and page 1 tie_fire_try loads it again from the shot table. the frame mask in front of it is 0, so every frame counts

P3:8C51.name: CPUMVL
P3:8C51.desc: Star Wars' CPUMVL (move locally), the same code with ESB's record offsets, which is why the matcher missed it: unless the ship of S1_PRM is glowing from a hit (byte 7) its velocity is cleared and built again from the move flags AS_CHMV of the current choreography step, one bit each for down, down twice, up, up twice, forward and forward twice (SNMVD to SNMVF2). DOAMOV then adds the velocity to the position

P3:8D25.name: chor_bad_op
P3:8D25.desc: choreography opcodes 6 and 7, which are not assigned: jumps to NWCHOR, which starts the step at AS_CHPC again. Star Wars has CHERR here, a SWI. no table on this page holds such an opcode, and one would loop for ever since the step is never passed over

P3:8D85.name: NWNSHP_P3
P3:8D85.desc: Star Wars' NWNSHP (new alien ships) without its first instruction, the JSR INOBJ, which is why the matcher missed it. picks the set of wave lists for the TIE fighter level SP_WAV from TSPWAV_P3 (past the sixth set the last two take turns), takes the list for level WV_LVL of the set into WV_LP, clears WV_LIV and the three alien records and makes a ship with NWASHP for each entry of the list, three at most. called by tie_wave_init

P3:9371.name: tie_setup_copy
P3:9371.desc: not reached on this page. from $9361 to $9560 page 3 holds the same bytes as page 2 (and from $9472 on as page 0): a copy of the code at P3_8613-P3_87FF assembled at other addresses. this routine is man_tie_setup again and SNVW and S2VW follow it. its JSR $9A1A is NWCHOR on page 0, on this page it lands in the middle of xmit_trail_shift, and its choreography address $9C56 does not fit this page either. no maze entry and no code of page 3 calls it

P3:95D3.name: view_lazars
P3:95D3.desc: ESB's form of Star Wars' VWLAZ (view lazars), rewritten around a table: nothing unless LZ_ON or LZ_HIT is set. takes the gun positions of the player's craft from lz_gun_tab (8 bytes for each craft_type 0-2, a higher type is put back to 0) and draws the beams of one side with LAZVW, the left guns when LZ_ALT is odd and the right ones when it is even. craft type 0 has one gun a side, types 1 and 2 a second pair, whose entry is $18 bytes further on. for each beam it writes the blank vector to the gun (its position plus the gun shift LZ_GY, LZ_GX) and leaves the distance from there to the sight in TMPDY and TMPDX. Y is the display list, X and U are kept

P3:97CB.name: lz_hit_walker
P3:97CB.desc: lazar collision test of the walker part, called by vew_walker and vew_walker_end after everything is drawn, the walker form of lz_hit_probot. does nothing while LZ_ON is 0. an enemy shot (CL_GDS) nearer than the AT-AT (atat_hit_d) and the AT-ST (atst_hit_d) under the cursor is hit through GNHTSG on page 1, a call, so the walker test still follows. then the nearer of the two walkers is hit with LZ_HIT = 4, an AT-AT through page 0 P0_9003 and an AT-ST through page 1 atst_killed. when the record word that goes with the distance is 0 the lazar only splashes at that distance (P3_9817)

4C97.name: lz_sw_edge
4C97.desc: fire switch bits that turned the lazars on in this frame: TSTLAZ clears it, then copies VG_LON (the switch edges the IRQ collected) into it when that is not 0. page 0 P0_969D, the walker part's tow cable view, tests bits $30 of it

esb_notes.P3:868B: the Darth Vader speeches are gone and the ship is drawn through bank 1 (BJCNTR, JOBJBPNT, KDA2C, KD8AC). the record fields from the picture number on are one byte further on than in Star Wars
esb_notes.P3:89AC: the Darth Vader score is gone, and Star Wars' XPSA is in line at the end (P3_8A31): it counts WV_LIV down, frees the record and starts the explosion through bank 1 KE57C, scores 100 points while bonus_left is running and 1,000 after, and the kill that brings bonus_left to 0 scores the 5,000 point bonus, awards the Jedi letter (page 1 P1_9573) and raises quota_tie
esb_notes.P3:8A6A: after CPUAL each live ship also has its fire delay counted down (tie_fire_delay)
esb_notes.P3:8A93: runs for the end of the TIE fighter part (phe_tie_flee, phase $28): the ships close in on the centre line and race away ahead of the player until their x overflows, then their records are freed. there is no Death Star to go back to
esb_notes.P3:8AEE: the shot itself is left to page 1 tie_fire, called once the ship's fire delay (byte 4 of the record) has run out, which takes the place of Star Wars' probability table TGPROB and its search for a free gun. carry set on return means a shot was started
esb_notes.P3:8DE0: the record fields sit one byte further on than in Star Wars from the picture number on, since ESB put the fire delay at byte 4: picture 5, dying 6, glow 7, hits 8, damage 9, forced roll 10, aim 11, target 12. the object is loaded by bank 1 KD868 through L60A8
esb_notes.P3:8E27: here the object is loaded too: the routine ends with the call of bank 1 KD868 (L60A8) that Star Wars' ADASHP leaves out. called by wave3_exec while fewer than three ships are alive
esb_notes.P3:93D2: part of the stale copy at $9361-$9560 (see tie_setup_copy): the same bytes as SNVW on page 2, not reached on this page, where the maze calls SNVW_P3 at $8674
esb_notes.P3:93E9: part of the stale copy at $9361-$9560, cut off after 10 words of its colour table by TSTLAZ at $9561. only its last instructions matter on this page: lz_hit_probot and lz_hit_space read $9548 and $9540 to put the slapstic in its bitwise mode
esb_notes.P3:9561: ESB also copies the fire switch bits to lz_sw_edge, picks the lazar sound by wave_type (aud_cmd_4d in the probot and walker parts, aud_cmd_3f in the two space parts, the force flag Q_FRC is gone) and resets the distances of its own targets: probot, transmission, AT-AT, AT-ST and asteroid

questions: P3:91BD, P3:9244, P3:924A-P3:9253, P3:9268 and P3:92DD: every twirl step of the choreography tables has half its Star Wars time (first byte n*4+4 where Star Wars has n*8+4). for Star Wars' .CT 80 that gives $80 and for .CT 01 it gives $08, and CHOPDO decodes by the low three bits, so these steps run as CHIF_D (an if on the twirl and move bytes taken as a status mask) and not as twirls: the long rolls of 1D1, 1D2 and 1BZ and the first step of SPLIT are skipped or branch on the random bits. described as the code runs, it looks like an oversight of the time change, not checked in the running game

P3:8EA0 and P3:8EA4 show the operands AS_ROL,X and AS_GLW,X. ESB's alien record has a new byte 4 (fire delay), so every field from the picture number on is one byte further on than in Star Wars: 5 picture, 6 dying, 7 glow, 8 hits left, 9 damage, 10 forced roll, 11 aim, 12 target. the defines still give AS_ROL = 9 and AS_GLW = 6, the Star Wars offsets, and these two lines (and P0_9BE7, P0_9BEB on page 0) are their only uses, where they name the wrong field. the generator's sw_drop_symbols (AS_ROL, AS_GLW) would turn them back into plain offsets, I did not use that key since the brief does not list it and put comments on the two lines instead

P3:9118, P3:9130 and P3:9133 carried the Star Wars labels TCH1BZ, TCH2C1 and TCH1C1. by the wave lists that point at them (TWV1A/2A use $909D-$9118, TWV1B/2B use $9130-$91A5) and by their steps they are TCH1AZ, TCH2B1 and TCH1B1: ESB's halved times make TCH1B1 byte for byte like Star Wars' TCH1C1. I listed the three addresses in sw_drop_names although they are data labels, not routines, and gave the right names in labels. the carried comment .CGOTO TCH1BZ at P3_9115 is dropped for the same reason. the comments .CT 10,... on P3_9133-P3_913C come from Star Wars' TCH1C1 as well, they give the right flags and I left them

P3:8A7B carried the label NWNSHP_90_P3, but it is the loop end of CPU (Star Wars CPU_40), the real NWNSHP_90 is P3_8DD5 (shown as NWNSHP_90_P3_2). listed in sw_drop_names with the new label CPU_40_P3. the label IPGEN_30 at P3_85FE is on the instruction Star Wars has it on, but ESB's loop starts two instructions earlier at P3_85F8

all table names in labels are Atari's Star Wars names with _P3 added, since pages 0 and 2 hold older copies of the same tables. many of them (and tie_copy_tail at P3_9361) fall inside .byte rows of the snapshot, so the rows have to be split there. the choreography steps are a byte and a word or three bytes, no region kind fits them and they stay .byte
P3:8664 LDD #$908B and P3:93C2 LDD #$9C56 load choreography addresses and show as plain constants. the first should read man_tie_chor

P3:9361-P3:9560: page 3 has the same bytes as page 2 from $9361 and as page 0 from $9472, and all four pages are the same from $952B. on this page nothing reaches them (P3_9371 is an orphan, the maze calls SNVW_P3 at $8674). the listing shows $9371-$954B as code under the names SNVW_P3_2 and S2VW_P3_2, it might be better shown as .byte with a note. P3_9560 ($D6) is the last byte of the copy

P3:96C5 and P3:96DD: craft type 2 is accepted by view_lazars but nothing found sets craft_type to 2. its second pair is the Star Wars upper guns (x -390 and 390, y -104), its first pair has a sight y word of -143 where the pattern of the other entries (screen y + 104) would give -413, so its beams would not end on the sight
P3:8613: man_init_tie loads B with the manual page before the call, the routine overwrites B at once. the three TIE fighter pages of the manual get the same set-up

P3:97E4: the hit of an enemy shot is a call (JSR through the maze) and the walker tests follow it, where lz_hit_probot and lz_hit_space jump. so in the walker part one frame can hit a shot and a walker behind it. described as the code runs

$4C05, $4C07, $4C09, $4C0D, $4C11 and $4C15 in this range already have names in notes p3_9800.json and p1_8c00.json (atat_hit_d, atat_hit_rec, xmit_hit_d, atst_hit_d, astr_hit_d, and for $4C0D both prob_hit_d there and prb_aim_dep in a page 2 file, which the loader reports as a clash). I used atat_hit_d and atst_hit_d in my text and gave none of them an entry here
P3:97C9 is typed as one word ($A001, VJLZF0, the JSRL to lazar fire slot 0). TLZFR itself is already shown as words
